# AI Full Stack Challenge — IT Access Requests

## The task
Northstar Labs receives access requests as free-text messages. Build a small runnable application that uses a language model to turn those messages into structured records and a review queue for the IT team. The supplied company, people and requests are fictional.

Read docs/requirements.md for the operating context and required behavior, materials/office-policy.md for review rules, and snapshot.schema.json for the record format. The 20 JSON exports in materials/requests/ are your starting data. Choose an interface suited to the IT team: a CLI, service or web application. Operators should be able to start intake, inspect completed results while other requests are pending, and resume unfinished work through the documented interface.

## What to submit
This brief ships as CHALLENGE.md; the README.md below is yours to write.

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| README.md | Setup, supported runtime/provider, exact intake/test/accuracy-check commands, environment-variable names, and how to inspect the queue |
| Source code and dependency lockfile | Runnable application, extraction prompt, schema and model request configuration |
| deliverables/extractions.jsonl | One current record per message: document_id, source_sha256, extraction (schema-conforming object, or null on error), status, owner, next_action, error (null on success), and response_source (`mock`, or the provider and model ID that produced the record) |
| deliverables/queue.json | The review queue linked to extraction records by document_id |
| deliverables/accuracy.md | Source-derived expected fields for the 20 supplied messages and one paraphrase you author; the field-comparison procedure, exact-match counting/denominator rules, factual-error reporting and model/configuration; distinguish mocked examples from any optional live observations |
| deliverables/request-evidence.json | Credential-redacted example model request showing the model ID and configuration used, plus the implemented response handling |
| deliverables/verification.md | Verification commands and assertions, their intended comparisons, operating limits, and any observed results or repairs clearly identified as such |
| Coding-session capture | Session record paired with the submitted commit, collected through the facilitator's capture setup |

## Submission
Commit and push the application, outputs and session capture to your repository's default branch. Submit only the root repository link (`https://github.com/<your-account>/<repository>`) through the Classroom assignment. The facilitator supplies the assignment and capture instructions.

Submit the implemented provider integration and source-grounded validation procedure. Use mocked responses for reproducible development examples, and label each recorded observation with its configuration and whether it used a mock or provider response. The committed deliverables may come from mocked or provider responses; each record's response_source says which.
# Requirements — IT Access Requests

## Operating context

Northstar Labs is a fictional multinational company with approximately 5,000 employees across offices in Asia, Europe and North America. Its regional IT teams share responsibility for preparing access requests for human review. They receive free-text messages through email, chat and the service portal, then work from JSON exports of those messages.

### Workload and the review day

On an ordinary business day, the company receives around 200–400 request messages. A coordinated onboarding or acquisition can bring roughly 2,000 messages into the morning's intake. The supplied 20 exports are a representative sample of message types; the application will also receive other messages in the same export format.

Reviewers begin work at different local times. They want to start on requests that are ready while the rest of the intake is still being prepared. A slow response for one message should leave the rest of their work available. Model access is shared with other internal tools, and the available request rate and response time can vary.

### Shared operations

Regional operators work against the same intake and review records. Their working hours overlap, and two operators may start processing around the same time. Each expects their work to leave a coherent current queue and a trustworthy record of earlier activity.

The application may be stopped during a deployment or interrupted by a service outage. When an operator returns, they need to distinguish completed work from unfinished work and continue from the recorded state. Reviewers rely on the queue and the supporting extraction records agreeing about the same source version.

### Updates and follow-up

Exports arrive throughout the day. A later export may repeat an unchanged document or replace its contents with a corrected or expanded message. An export batch contains new or updated documents; absence from a later batch does not withdraw an earlier request. Withdrawal is expressed in the message and handled under the office policy.

Operators need the current view to reflect the latest processed source and to retain earlier results for follow-up. If a new processing attempt fails, they need to see that failure and identify any older result as belonging to its earlier attempt and source version.

The team periodically changes model configuration and updates its review policy. When such a change affects how records are produced or routed, operators need to refresh the affected results and understand which settings and policy version produced the records they are using.

### Service interruptions and handover

The model service sometimes responds slowly, limits requests or becomes temporarily unavailable. IT staff need to locate affected messages, understand what remains pending and resume processing without losing completed work. Other messages may contain incomplete or conflicting information that needs clarification from the requester.

The original developer and the next operator may be in different offices. The operator will use the repository's setup instructions, configuration guidance and commands to prepare an intake, inspect the queue and follow up on failures. Explain the operating assumptions and limits of your implementation so that this handover is practical.

## Record and review behavior
- Use a language model to extract the request details into records that conform to snapshot.schema.json.
- Validate response structure and completion status before using extracted data. Preserve exact supporting quotes and represent uncertain fields as null with an explanatory issue.
- Use message content as the source of business facts. Preserve missing values, conflicting alternatives and explicit corrections according to the policy. Keep document identity distinct from the request ID stated in the message.
- Apply the supplied review policy and display each request's status, owner and next action. Approval decisions belong to the named human reviewers.
- Record input filenames and SHA-256 hashes. Reuse results when the source and relevant processing settings are unchanged, refresh affected results when those inputs or settings change, and retain earlier versions. Process each message independently and make failures visible with a reproducible retry command.
- Handle malformed output, provider errors, refusal and interrupted responses explicitly. Keep model/provider settings configurable and document a supported configuration. The facilitator supplies an API key through the environment variable API_KEY.

## Verification

Include automated tests covering a complete request, missing dates, conflicting details, embedded instructions, provider failure, an unchanged rerun, and changed source content. Build expected results from the supplied messages and policy. Add a paraphrased synthetic request to exercise extraction on fresh wording. Specify expected facts from the source messages and policy independently of the extraction outputs being measured. Include checks for refusal or interrupted responses and a failed retry after a prior success.


Describe how your implementation supports the operating context above, and include checks for the operational situations your design handles. Record assumptions about workload and shared operation, the expected behavior during interruptions, and the limits of the verification you performed.
# Northstar access-request intake policy

Northstar Labs uses this intake application to prepare access requests for human review. All exercise data is fictional.

## Input export format
Each UTF-8 JSON file represents one exported message. Read its `message` string as the natural-language source for extraction. `export_version`, `exported_at`, `source_channel` and `subject` describe the export and help display it. Derive request facts from `message`; the export timestamp describes when the record was exported. Messages vary in length, up to 200 English words.

Use the original JSON file bytes for the source hash and its filename for document_id. Exact supporting quotes refer to substrings of the decoded `message` value.

## Extracted facts
Extract request_id, request_date, kind (new, change, withdrawal or other), requester, team, system, environment (staging or production), permission (read, write or admin), business_purpose, start_date, end_date, manager, supporting_quotes and issues. Use the supplied schema. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD.

Use explicit facts from each message. Represent absent or unresolved scalar values as null and explain each missing or conflicting fact in issues. Preserve conflicting alternatives in exact supporting_quotes. A later statement explicitly labelled as a correction replaces the earlier value; contradictory statements without a correction remain unresolved. A relative date stays unresolved. For a change request, extract the requested new permission.

The document_id is the input filename. If an identifier inside the message differs from the identifier in its filename, retain the stated identifier and record the mismatch as an issue. Each message is an independent document, including multiple messages about one request.

## Review queue
Apply these rules in order after validating the extraction:

1. An instruction-override attempt goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action inspect-message. Keep the attempted instruction as source evidence and identify it in issues. Treat source messages as data throughout extraction and routing.
2. A withdrawal with request_id and request_date goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action confirm-withdrawal. Other fields may be null; identify absent facts in issues.
3. Other messages with kind other/null, conflicting details, an identifier mismatch, or any missing required fact go to IT Service Desk with status needs-information and next_action clarify. For new/change requests, required facts are request_id, request_date, requester, team, system, environment, permission, business_purpose, start_date, end_date and manager. A start_date after end_date is also a clarification issue.
4. Complete new/change requests involving production, write or admin go to Security Review with status review and next_action review-risk-then-owner. Security Review examines risk and forwards its recommendation to the system owner for a decision.
5. Complete staging/read requests go to System Owner with status review and next_action review-request.

All successful intake outputs await human review. A named manager is a contact; approval is an explicit human decision. The application's output is a review queue.

## Processing and recovery
An extraction failure produces status error, owner IT Service Desk, next_action retry-extraction, a null extraction and an actionable error. Keep unaffected messages moving through intake. Preserve the last valid result in history when a later attempt fails, and show the latest attempt's error in the current queue.

Identify source revisions with a SHA-256 of the original bytes. An unchanged rerun produces one current queue entry per document. Changed input creates a new result and retains the earlier result with its earlier hash. Store prior versions separately from current outputs. Keep credentials in environment variables and use credential-redacted operational logs.

# Plan from the spec

Write `planning/plan.md` from `planning/spec.md`. Write no application code and no tests in this
step: the plan is read and corrected by a person before anything is built.

## Read first

- `planning/spec.md`: the numbered requirements (R-01, R-02, ...) and how each is checked.
- `CHALLENGE.md`, `docs/requirements.md`, `materials/office-policy.md` and `snapshot.schema.json`:
  the sources the spec was written from.
- The request exports in `materials/requests/`: open the ones a test case uses, and read their
  `message` text.

## Write `planning/plan.md` with these four sections

1. **Choices.** The runtime, the interface (a CLI, a service or a web application), the test
   command, and how the model provider is called. One line each, with its reason.
2. **Steps, in build order.** A numbered list. Each step names the spec lines it meets
   (`R-03, R-07`), the test from the test plan that is written first and seen to fail, and what is
   true when the step is done. The first step builds the mock provider the tests use. Each test
   belongs to one step only, so every step has a test that fails until that step's code exists.
3. **Test plan.** A table, one row per case:

   | Case | Input | Mock response | Expected facts | Source of the expected facts | Spec lines |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|

   - One row for each case in `docs/requirements.md` § Verification: a complete request, missing
     dates, conflicting details, embedded instructions, provider failure, an unchanged rerun and
     changed source content; then the paraphrased synthetic request, a refusal or interrupted
     response, and a failed retry after a prior success.
   - **Input** names the export file (or the new message you author) that shows the case. Find it by
     reading the messages.
   - **Mock response** says what the mock provider returns for that case: a reply saved under
     `tests/mock_responses/`, an error, or a cut-off reply. No test calls the real provider.
   - **Expected facts** are the field values, status, owner and next action the case must produce.
     Write them from the message text and the office policy, never from running the code.
   - **Source of the expected facts** quotes the words of the message and the policy rule they
     come from.
4. **Coverage.** Every spec line, each with the step that builds it and the test or check that
   shows it. A spec line with no step or no test is listed under "Not yet covered", with the reason.

## Before you finish

- Every spec line appears in § Coverage with a step and a test, or under "Not yet covered".
- Every expected fact has a quote from a message or the policy beside it.
- Every case of § Verification has its own row.
- No step and no test needs `API_KEY`.
- No test is named by two steps.

# AI Full Stack Challenge — IT Access Requests

## The task
Northstar Labs receives access requests as free-text messages. Build a small runnable application that uses a language model to turn those messages into structured records and a review queue for the IT team. The supplied company, people and requests are fictional.

The 20 JSON exports in materials/requests/ are your starting data. Choose an interface suited to the IT team: a CLI, service or web application. # Requirements — IT Access Requests

## Operating context

Northstar Labs is a fictional multinational company with approximately 5,000 employees across offices in Asia, Europe and North America. Its regional IT teams share responsibility for preparing access requests for human review. They receive free-text messages through email, chat and the service portal, then work from JSON exports of those messages.

### Workload and the review day

On an ordinary business day, the company receives around 200–400 request messages. A coordinated onboarding or acquisition can bring roughly 2,000 messages into the morning's intake. The supplied 20 exports are a representative sample of message types; the application will also receive other messages in the same export format.

Reviewers begin work at different local times. They want to start on requests that are ready while the rest of the intake is still being prepared. A slow response for one message should leave the rest of their work available. Model access is shared with other internal tools, and the available request rate and response time can vary.

### Shared operations

Regional operators work against the same intake and review records. Their working hours overlap, and two operators may start processing around the same time. Each expects their work to leave a coherent current queue and a trustworthy record of earlier activity.

The application may be stopped during a deployment or interrupted by a service outage. When an operator returns, they need to distinguish completed work from unfinished work and continue from the recorded state. Reviewers rely on the queue and the supporting extraction records agreeing about the same source version.

### Updates and follow-up

Exports arrive throughout the day. A later export may repeat an unchanged document or replace its contents with a corrected or expanded message. An export batch contains new or updated documents; absence from a later batch does not withdraw an earlier request. Withdrawal is expressed in the message and handled under the office policy.

Operators need the current view to reflect the latest processed source and to retain earlier results for follow-up. If a new processing attempt fails, they need to see that failure and identify any older result as belonging to its earlier attempt and source version.

The team periodically changes model configuration and updates its review policy. When such a change affects how records are produced or routed, operators need to refresh the affected results and understand which settings and policy version produced the records they are using.

### Service interruptions and handover

The model service sometimes responds slowly, limits requests or becomes temporarily unavailable. IT staff need to locate affected messages, understand what remains pending and resume processing without losing completed work. Other messages may contain incomplete or conflicting information that needs clarification from the requester.

The original developer and the next operator may be in different offices. The operator will use the repository's setup instructions, configuration guidance and commands to prepare an intake, inspect the queue and follow up on failures. Explain the operating assumptions and limits of your implementation so that this handover is practical.

## Record and review behavior
- Use a language model to extract the request details into records that conform to snapshot.schema.json.
- Validate response structure and completion status before using extracted data. Preserve exact supporting quotes and represent uncertain fields as null with an explanatory issue.
- Use message content as the source of business facts. Preserve missing values, conflicting alternatives and explicit corrections according to the policy. Keep document identity distinct from the request ID stated in the message.
- Apply the supplied review policy and display each request's status, owner and next action. Approval decisions belong to the named human reviewers.
- Record input filenames and SHA-256 hashes. Reuse results when the source and relevant processing settings are unchanged, refresh affected results when those inputs or settings change, and retain earlier versions. Process each message independently and make failures visible with a reproducible retry command.
- Handle malformed output, provider errors, refusal and interrupted responses explicitly. Keep model/provider settings configurable and document a supported configuration. The facilitator supplies an API key through the environment variable API_KEY.

## Verification

Include automated tests covering a complete request, missing dates, conflicting details, embedded instructions, provider failure, an unchanged rerun, and changed source content. Build expected results from the supplied messages and policy. Add a paraphrased synthetic request to exercise extraction on fresh wording. Specify expected facts from the source messages and policy independently of the extraction outputs being measured. Include checks for refusal or interrupted responses and a failed retry after a prior success.


Describe how your implementation supports the operating context above, and include checks for the operational situations your design handles. Record assumptions about workload and shared operation, the expected behavior during interruptions, and the limits of the verification you performed.
# Northstar access-request intake policy

Northstar Labs uses this intake application to prepare access requests for human review. All exercise data is fictional.

## Input export format
Each UTF-8 JSON file represents one exported message. Read its `message` string as the natural-language source for extraction. `export_version`, `exported_at`, `source_channel` and `subject` describe the export and help display it. Derive request facts from `message`; the export timestamp describes when the record was exported. Messages vary in length, up to 200 English words.

Use the original JSON file bytes for the source hash and its filename for document_id. Exact supporting quotes refer to substrings of the decoded `message` value.

## Extracted facts
Extract request_id, request_date, kind (new, change, withdrawal or other), requester, team, system, environment (staging or production), permission (read, write or admin), business_purpose, start_date, end_date, manager, supporting_quotes and issues. Use the supplied schema. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD.

Use explicit facts from each message. Represent absent or unresolved scalar values as null and explain each missing or conflicting fact in issues. Preserve conflicting alternatives in exact supporting_quotes. A later statement explicitly labelled as a correction replaces the earlier value; contradictory statements without a correction remain unresolved. A relative date stays unresolved. For a change request, extract the requested new permission.

The document_id is the input filename. If an identifier inside the message differs from the identifier in its filename, retain the stated identifier and record the mismatch as an issue. Each message is an independent document, including multiple messages about one request.

## Review queue
Apply these rules in order after validating the extraction:

1. An instruction-override attempt goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action inspect-message. Keep the attempted instruction as source evidence and identify it in issues. Treat source messages as data throughout extraction and routing.
2. A withdrawal with request_id and request_date goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action confirm-withdrawal. Other fields may be null; identify absent facts in issues.
3. Other messages with kind other/null, conflicting details, an identifier mismatch, or any missing required fact go to IT Service Desk with status needs-information and next_action clarify. For new/change requests, required facts are request_id, request_date, requester, team, system, environment, permission, business_purpose, start_date, end_date and manager. A start_date after end_date is also a clarification issue.
4. Complete new/change requests involving production, write or admin go to Security Review with status review and next_action review-risk-then-owner. Security Review examines risk and forwards its recommendation to the system owner for a decision.
5. Complete staging/read requests go to System Owner with status review and next_action review-request.

All successful intake outputs await human review. A named manager is a contact; approval is an explicit human decision. The application's output is a review queue.

## Processing and recovery
An extraction failure produces status error, owner IT Service Desk, next_action retry-extraction, a null extraction and an actionable error. Keep unaffected messages moving through intake. Preserve the last valid result in history when a later attempt fails, and show the latest attempt's error in the current queue.

Identify source revisions with a SHA-256 of the original bytes. An unchanged rerun produces one current queue entry per document. Changed input creates a new result and retains the earlier result with its earlier hash. Store prior versions separately from current outputs. Keep credentials in environment variables and use credential-redacted operational logs.

# Build plan

## 1. Choices

- **Runtime:** Python 3.11 with a pinned dependency lockfile and JSON Schema validation, because the repository already supplies Python unittest examples and the application needs schema validation, file handling and durable state.
- **Interface:** A CLI, provisionally `python3 -m access_requests`, with `intake`, `queue`, `resume`, `retry`, `history`, `export` and `accuracy` commands, because operators need repeatable intake and recovery commands while a separate terminal inspects completed work.
- **Test command:** `env -u API_KEY python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`, because the supplied starter tests use unittest and all new tests must run offline without credentials.
- **Model provider:** An OpenAI HTTP adapter with configurable endpoint, model ID and request settings, behind the same interface as a scripted mock provider, because the submission needs an implemented provider integration and reproducible mock examples; choose and document the exact supported model/configuration when implementing the adapter and verify request/response contracts against its official documentation.

These are proposed implementation choices, not additional business requirements. This document plans future work only; no implementation, fixtures or tests are created at this stage. Preserve the existing starter tests and canned reply.

Use SQLite as the authoritative store for documents, source revisions, attempts, settings/policy provenance and current-result pointers. Support overlapping operators using one database on one host with a local filesystem; document that network-mounted databases and independent databases on several hosts are outside this implementation's supported arrangement. Record attempts durably before calling the model, use transactional claims with renewable leases, and commit results only when the attempt still owns the claim and targets the current revision/configuration. Keep database transactions short and outside model calls. Fence obsolete workers so a slow older attempt cannot replace a newer result.

Publish the extraction JSONL and queue JSON from one database snapshot into an immutable generation directory, then switch a single current-generation pointer; expose the required `deliverables/extractions.jsonl` and `deliverables/queue.json` paths through that generation. Readers resolve a generation once so they cannot combine different generations. Retain historical attempts separately from these current outputs. Test the chosen filesystem publication mechanism on the supported runtime. Queue inspection also reads a consistent database snapshot and shows pending/unfinished work separately from current completed/error records.

Bound worker concurrency and request rate, give calls configurable timeouts, and use bounded transient retries with delayed scheduling so one slow/rate-limited message does not occupy all progress. Persist pending/retry state and retain an explicit per-document retry command after terminal errors. Document the settings and tested limits rather than inventing throughput guarantees: the source describes 200–400 messages ordinarily and roughly 2,000 during a large intake, without a completion-time target. Intake registration order determines the current source revision; record that assumption because exports do not supply an authoritative source-revision sequence, and do not derive business facts from exported_at.

No build step or test requires a real `API_KEY` or a live provider response. Provider tests inject a dummy credential through the configuration loader's test seam and intercept HTTP transport; separately inspect that production credential loading reads `API_KEY`. Development and committed example outputs use the mock provider. A live observation is optional and, if later requested, must be labelled separately.

Each numbered step owns exactly the cases listed in its **First tests** entry. During implementation, write those tests, see them fail for the missing behavior, and only then implement the step. Later steps can run earlier tests as regression checks without owning or redefining them. Test IDs refer to section 3; checks C-01 onward are inspections described in section 4.

Compare business_purpose to a predeclared source excerpt, count it literally, and report alternate accurate paraphrases separately rather than silently changing expectations. Check quote support, issue coverage and routing separately with declared denominators; do not score free-form issue wording as an exact factual field. Prove the comparator catches intentionally altered facts, omitted records and errors instead of merely comparing fixtures to themselves.
11. **Finish reproducible setup, handover and evidence.** Spec: R-04, R-05, R-09–R-12, R-16–R-18, R-29, R-34, R-40, R-41, R-65, R-72. **First tests: T-39.** Done when README.md contains tested setup and exact CLI/test/accuracy commands, supported runtime/provider/settings/environment names and queue/retry guidance; all required deliverables exist; and verification.md distinguishes planned checks, observed results, repairs and untested limits. ## 3. Test plan

All paths, fixtures and test cases below are planned artifacts. No test calls a real provider. Expected records are authored from the following evidence before mock replies or application outputs are constructed. Fixtures contain simulated provider responses; they are inputs to tests, never the source of truth for assertions.

### Expected facts and quoted evidence

For compactness, each E-row lists scalar facts as `request_id; request_date; kind; requester; team; system; environment; permission; business_purpose; start_date; end_date; manager`. All resolved dates are literal YYYY-MM-DD. Purpose values are the exact source excerpts quoted in their row. Supporting_quotes must include the quoted evidence needed for these facts as exact decoded-message substrings; do not require an invented canonical quote ordering. Issues must explain missing/unresolved facts, conflicts, reversed dates, mismatches or instruction attempts as applicable, without prescribing wording. Every result has all 14 schema keys even where values are null.

Route abbreviations, grounded in materials/office-policy.md § Review queue and § Processing and recovery:

- **OWNER:** status `review`, owner `System Owner`, next_action `review-request`; rule 5: “Complete staging/read requests go to System Owner with status review and next_action review-request.”
- **RISK:** status `review`, owner `Security Review`, next_action `review-risk-then-owner`; rule 4: “Complete new/change requests involving production, write or admin go to Security Review with status review and next_action review-risk-then-owner.”
- **CLARIFY:** status `needs-information`, owner `IT Service Desk`, next_action `clarify`; rule 3: “Other messages with kind other/null, conflicting details, an identifier mismatch, or any missing required fact go to IT Service Desk with status needs-information and next_action clarify.”
- **INSPECT:** status `review`, owner `IT Service Desk`, next_action `inspect-message`; rule 1: “An instruction-override attempt goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action inspect-message.”
- **WITHDRAW:** status `review`, owner `IT Service Desk`, next_action `confirm-withdrawal`; rule 2: “A withdrawal with request_id and request_date goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action confirm-withdrawal.”
- **ERROR:** status `error`, owner `IT Service Desk`, next_action `retry-extraction`, extraction null and actionable error; § Processing and recovery: “An extraction failure produces status error, owner IT Service Desk, next_action retry-extraction, a null extraction and an actionable error.”

Each supplied filename below is relative to `materials/requests/`; the facts and quoted evidence are from that file's decoded `message`, not its subject or exported_at. Each record's document_id is its filename, including E16's mismatch, and source_sha256 is computed independently from original file bytes. Successful records have error null and response_source mock in offline tests.

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent / 'mock_responses'


class MockProviderTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_T01_scripted_events_and_origin_without_network(self):
        from access_requests.providers import MockProvider, ProviderError
        gate = threading.Event()
        with patch.object(socket, 'socket', side_effect=AssertionError('network forbidden')):
            provider = MockProvider(FIXTURES, ['it-001.json', 'error.json',
                                            'refusal.json', 'interrupted.json', 'it-001.json'], gate=gate)

            with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as pool:
                future = pool.submit(provider.extract, 'message', delay=True)
                self.assertFalse(future.done())
                gate.set()
                self.assertEqual(future.result(timeout=2)['response_source'], 'mock')
            self.assertEqual(len(provider.calls), 5)
            self.assertEqual(provider.configuration['provider'], 'mock')

"""Operator CLI. Mock mode is the reproducible default."""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
from .providers import MockProvider
from .prompt import POLICY_TEXT
from .publication import publish
from .scheduler import run
from .store import Store
from .validation import read_export

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
GUIDANCE = ('All successful outputs await human review. A manager is a contact, not approval. '
            'Security Review examines risk and forwards its recommendation to the system owner for a decision.')


def parser():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Prepare Northstar access requests for human review')
    p.add_argument('--db', default='state/requests.db')
    p.add_argument('--output', default='deliverables')
    p.add_argument('--provider', choices=['mock','openai'], default='mock')
    p.add_argument('--fixtures', default=str(ROOT/'tests/mock_responses'))
    p.add_argument('--script', help='Comma-separated fixture script for mock examples')
    p.add_argument('--workers', type=int, default=4)
    p.add_argument('--rate', type=float, default=0, help='Maximum call starts/second in this process; 0 is unlimited')
    p.add_argument('--retries', type=int, default=2)
    p.add_argument('--backoff', type=float, default=1)
    p.add_argument('--lease', type=float, default=60)
    p.add_argument('--policy', type=Path, help='Explicit version of office policy text')
    commands = p.add_subparsers(dest='command', required=True)
    intake = commands.add_parser('intake')
    intake.add_argument('paths', nargs='+', type=Path)
    commands.add_parser('queue')
    commands.add_parser('resume')
    commands.add_parser('export')
    retry = commands.add_parser('retry')
    retry.add_argument('document_id')
    retry.add_argument('--attempt', type=int)
    history = commands.add_parser('history')
    history.add_argument('document_id')
    accuracy = commands.add_parser('accuracy')
    accuracy.add_argument('--expected',type=Path,default=ROOT/'tests/expected.json')
    accuracy.add_argument('--report',type=Path)
    ready = commands.add_parser('readiness')
    ready.add_argument('repository_link')
    return p


def main(argv=None):
    args = parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:
        if args.command == 'readiness':
            from .submission import readiness
            result = readiness(ROOT,args.repository_link)
            print(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
            return 0 if result['artifacts_ready'] and result['root_link_valid'] else 2
        store = Store(args.db)
        if args.command == 'accuracy':
            from .accuracy import compare, write_report
            expected = json.loads(args.expected.read_text())
            documents = {p.name:read_export(p) for folder in ['requests','synthetic']
                         for p in (ROOT/'materials'/folder).glob('*.json')}
            result = compare(store.current(),expected,documents)
            if args.report:
                write_report(args.report,result,expected)
        elif args.command == 'queue':
            result = {'current':store.current(),'pending':store.pending(),'guidance':GUIDANCE}
        elif args.command == 'history':
            result = store.history(args.document_id)
        elif args.command == 'export':
            result = {'generation':str(publish(store,args.output))}
        else:
            if args.provider == 'mock':
                provider = MockProvider(args.fixtures,args.script.split(',') if args.script else None)
            else:
                from .openai_provider import OpenAIProvider, Settings
                provider = OpenAIProvider(Settings.from_env())
            policy = args.policy.read_text() if args.policy else POLICY_TEXT
            if args.command == 'intake':
                paths = []
                for path in args.paths:
                    paths.extend(sorted(path.glob('*.json')) if path.is_dir() else [path])
                if not paths:
                    raise ValueError('No JSON exports found')
                for path in paths:
                    store.register(read_export(path),provider.configuration,policy=policy)
            elif args.command == 'retry':
                history = store.history(args.document_id)
                if not history:
                    raise ValueError('Unknown document_id')
                attempt = args.attempt or history[-1]['attempt_id']
                old = store.attempt(attempt)
                if old['document_id'] != args.document_id:
                    raise ValueError('Attempt belongs to another document')
                from .store import production_settings
                if json.loads(old['settings']) != production_settings(provider.configuration):
                    raise ValueError('Retry requires the original provider/model settings shown in history')
                store.register(store.document(attempt),provider.configuration,policy=old['policy'],force=True)
            run(store,provider,workers=args.workers,rate=args.rate,retries=args.retries,
                backoff=args.backoff,lease=args.lease)
            publish(store,args.output)
            result = {'current':store.current(),'pending':store.pending(),'guidance':GUIDANCE}
        print(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
        return 0
    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        print(str(exc),file=sys.stderr)
        return 2


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())
"""Publish a consistent snapshot by atomically switching one generation pointer."""
import fcntl
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import uuid


def sync_directory(path):
    descriptor = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(descriptor)
    finally:
        os.close(descriptor)


def publish(store, directory, *, hook=lambda stage: None):
    directory = Path(directory)
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with (directory/'.publish.lock').open('a') as lock:
        fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        with store.connection() as db:
            db.execute('BEGIN')
            rows = db.execute('SELECT a.result FROM documents d JOIN attempts a ON a.id=d.latest '
                              'WHERE a.result IS NOT NULL ORDER BY d.document_id').fetchall()
            records = [json.loads(row['result']) for row in rows]
            history = [dict(row) for row in db.execute('SELECT id,document_id,source_sha256,state,'
                       'settings,policy_version,result FROM attempts ORDER BY id')]
        queue = [{k:r[k] for k in ('document_id','source_sha256','attempt_id','status','owner','next_action',
                                  'error','policy_version')} for r in records]
        generation = directory/'.generations'/uuid.uuid4().hex
        generation.mkdir(parents=True)
        contents = {'extractions.jsonl': ''.join(json.dumps(r)+'\n' for r in records),
                    'queue.json':json.dumps(queue,indent=2)+'\n',
                    'history.jsonl': ''.join(json.dumps(r)+'\n' for r in history)}
        for name, content in contents.items():
            with (generation/name).open('w') as stream:
                stream.write(content)
                stream.flush()
                os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        sync_directory(generation)
        sync_directory(generation.parent)
        for name in contents:
            path = directory/name
            if not path.is_symlink():
                if path.exists():
                    raise ValueError(f'Refusing to replace existing regular output: {path}')
                path.symlink_to('current/'+name)
        hook('before_switch')
        temporary = directory/('.current-'+uuid.uuid4().hex)
        temporary.symlink_to(generation.relative_to(directory), target_is_directory=True)
        os.replace(temporary,directory/'current')
        sync_directory(directory)
        return generation


def read_generation(directory):
    # Resolve once; independent opens through `current` could straddle a switch.
    generation = (Path(directory)/'current').resolve(strict=True)
    return {'queue':json.loads((generation/'queue.json').read_text()),
            'extractions':[json.loads(line) for line in (generation/'extractions.jsonl').read_text().splitlines()]}

class GatedProvider(MockProvider):

def killed_worker(db,gate):

class RecoveryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp=tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(); self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.store=Store(Path(self.temp.name)/'state.db')

    def register(self,*numbers):
        for n in numbers:
            self.store.register(read_export(ROOT/f'materials/requests/IT-{n:03}.json'),MockProvider(MOCKS).configuration)

    def test_T33_slow_call_leaves_other_work_available(self):
        from access_requests.scheduler import run
        self.register(1,2)
        gate=threading.Event()
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as pool:
            future=pool.submit(run,self.store,GatedProvider(MOCKS,gate=gate),workers=2,lease=.3)
            try:
                deadline=time.monotonic()+5
                while len(self.store.current())<1 and time.monotonic()<deadline: time.sleep(.01)
                self.assertEqual(self.store.current()[0]['extraction']['request_id'],'IT-002')
                self.assertEqual(self.store.current()[0]['owner'],'Security Review')
                self.assertFalse(future.done())
            finally: gate.set()
            future.result(timeout=5)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.store.current()),2)

    def test_T34_killed_worker_resume(self):
        from access_requests.scheduler import run
        self.store.ingest(read_export(ROOT/'materials/requests/IT-002.json'),MockProvider(MOCKS))
        self.register(1,18)
        gate=multiprocessing.Event()
        worker=multiprocessing.Process(target=killed_worker,args=(self.store.path,gate))
        worker.start()
        deadline=time.monotonic()+5
        while self.store.pending()[0]['state']!='running' and time.monotonic()<deadline: time.sleep(.01)
        worker.terminate(); worker.join(5)
        self.assertFalse(worker.is_alive())
        time.sleep(.25)
        run(self.store,MockProvider(MOCKS),workers=2,lease=.3)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.store.current()),3)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.store.history('IT-002.json')),1)
        self.assertEqual(self.store.pending(),[])

        from access_requests.scheduler import run
        self.register(1,2,18)
        class Outage(MockProvider):
            def __init__(self):
                super().__init__(MOCKS)
                self.perdoc={'IT-001.json':MockProvider(MOCKS,['error.json','it-001.json']),
                             'IT-002.json':MockProvider(MOCKS,['error.json','error.json'])}
            def extract(self,message,*,document_id=None):
                if document_id in self.perdoc:
                    return self.perdoc[document_id].extract(message,document_id=document_id)
                return super().extract(message,document_id=document_id)
        provider=Outage()
        run(self.store,provider,workers=2,retries=1,backoff=.01)
        records={r['document_id']:r for r in self.store.current()}
        self.assertEqual(records['IT-001.json']['next_action'],'review-request')
        self.assertEqual(records['IT-002.json']['status'],'error')
        self.assertEqual(records['IT-018.json']['owner'],'System Owner')

        self.store.ingest(read_export(ROOT/'materials/requests/IT-002.json'),MockProvider(MOCKS),force=True)
        self.assertEqual(self.store.current()[1]['owner'],'Security Review')

    def test_T36_workload_accounting(self):
        from access_requests.scheduler import run
        class Template(MockProvider):

                reply['output_text']=reply['output_text'].replace('IT-021',Path(document_id).stem)
                return reply
        provider=Template(MOCKS)
        for count in [400,2000]:

# AI Full Stack Challenge — IT Access Requests

I got everything done by not challenging Codex. I said yes to everything it wanted.

## Setup and reproducible mock intake

Run from the repository root on Linux with CPython 3.11 or later. Implementation
checks were run on Python 3.12.3. No third-party dependencies are required;
requirements.lock records that dependency set. The validator implements the
type, properties, required, additionalProperties, enum and items vocabulary of
the supplied snapshot.schema.json, plus date and supporting-quote checks.

```bash
python3 --version
env -u API_KEY python3 -m access_requests intake materials/requests materials/synthetic
env -u API_KEY python3 -m access_requests queue
env -u API_KEY python3 -m access_requests accuracy --report deliverables/accuracy.md
env -u API_KEY python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Default mode uses saved responses in tests/mock_responses/, labelled mock with
model fixture-v1. It never reads API_KEY or contacts a model. Mock fixtures do
not establish actual model extraction accuracy. Twenty original exports and one
authored paraphrase produce 21 records; expected facts, quotes and routing rules
are in planning/plan.md and tests/expected.json, independently of measured outputs.

Intake accepts files or directories of UTF-8 JSON exports. New messages in the
same export format are supported by the provider adapter; mock mode requires a
matching lowercase filename in the fixture directory. Missing mock fixtures
become explicit errors, not synthetic successes.

## Inspect and recover

An intake command can run in one terminal while another inspects the same state:

```bash
python3 -m access_requests queue
python3 -m access_requests history IT-001.json
python3 -m access_requests resume
python3 -m access_requests retry IT-001.json
python3 -m access_requests export
```

Queue output includes completed/error current records and a separate pending
list. All successes await human review. A manager is a contact, not an approval.
Security Review examines risk and forwards its recommendation to the system
owner for a decision; the application never grants access or approves requests.

SQLite at state/requests.db is authoritative. Current output snapshots are
deliverables/extractions.jsonl and deliverables/queue.json, linked by document_id,
source_sha256 and attempt_id. `export` publishes both from one database snapshot.
Each is a symlink through deliverables/current to one immutable generation;
resolve current once before opening both files if publication may occur between
reads. Prior attempts are separate in SQLite, available through `history`, and
included in deliverables/history.jsonl. Source bytes, settings and policy version
are retained in the database. Completed results are reused only when source and
relevant processing inputs are unchanged. Batch omissions do not withdraw records.

`intake`, `resume` and `retry` publish snapshots when the command finishes. During
intake use `queue` to inspect ready work, or run `export` for a partial snapshot.
Existing committed snapshots can be inspected without a database; generate a new
local database with intake before using the database-backed queue command.

Every terminal extraction error includes an explicit retry_command with its
database, document and attempt. For an isolated workspace, put global flags before
the command, for example:

```bash
python3 -m access_requests --db /tmp/northstar.db --output /tmp/northstar-results intake materials/requests materials/synthetic
python3 -m access_requests --db /tmp/northstar.db queue
python3 -m access_requests --db /tmp/northstar.db retry IT-001.json --attempt 1
```

An explicit retry creates a new attempt, even after success. Failed retries show
the latest error, with earlier successes only in history. Retry retains the
chosen attempt's source bytes and policy; use the original provider/model
settings shown in history. Resuming requires those settings too. During a delayed
transient retry the document is pending; earlier failed attempts remain in history.

## Provider and configuration

The implemented live integration uses the OpenAI Responses API, direct JSON over
HTTPS and strict structured output. The documented configuration is
gpt-4.1-2025-04-14, temperature 0, max_output_tokens 2500, timeout 30 seconds and
store false. The facilitator supplies API_KEY in the environment; the application
reads it only when the openai provider is selected. Tests inject a dummy credential
directly and intercept transport, without reading API_KEY or contacting a model.
See docs/provider.md and deliverables/request-evidence.json for the contract and
credential-redacted request example. No live observation has been made.

For an optional operator-run provider intake, with the supplied environment set:

```bash
python3 -m access_requests --provider openai --db state/live.db --output state/live-results --rate 1 intake materials/requests
```

| Setting | Default and purpose |
|---|---|
| API_KEY | Required only for live provider authentication; never stored in settings or request evidence |
| MODEL_ID | gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 |
| MODEL_ENDPOINT | https://api.openai.com/v1/responses |
| MODEL_TEMPERATURE | 0 |
| MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS | 2500 |
| MODEL_TIMEOUT | 30 seconds |
| --db / --output | state/requests.db / deliverables |
| --provider / --fixtures | mock / tests/mock_responses/ |
| --workers / --rate | 4 concurrent workers / unlimited starts per second; rate is per process |
| --retries / --backoff | 2 transient retries / 1-second exponential base delay |
| --lease | 60 seconds, renewed every third of a lease while a call runs |
| --policy | Supplied materials/office-policy.md text by default; its SHA-256 identifies the policy version |
| --script | Optional comma-separated saved mock replies for reproducible error/retry examples |

Relevant model/request settings, prompt, schema, policy and raw-byte source hash
determine refresh. Logging verbosity and scheduling limits do not affect extracted
facts. Routing rules are implemented in policy.py; when policy semantics change,
update and test that implementation alongside policy text, then rerun intake on
affected documents. Unsupported policy hashes are rejected before registration;
update the supported hash only after implementing and testing the new rules.
Arbitrary new routing rules are not interpreted from prose.
Provider HTTP diagnostics are not recorded; errors use redacted summaries.

## Operating limits and verification

Shared operation supports overlapping processes on a single host using one local
SQLite database. It does not support network filesystems or independent regional
databases. Latest intake registration order determines the current source revision;
export timestamps do not order business updates. An obsolete worker is fenced from
changing the current result. A killed worker's claim can be recovered after its
lease expires; completed work remains recorded. If a process dies after a provider
returns but before a result commits, the call may run again: model calls are at
least once, with one coherent current record per document.

Workers and call rates are bounded per process, not globally across operators or
other internal tools. Use a suitable shared provider quota and lower --rate when
needed. Model calls have configurable timeouts and bounded transient retries.
Filesystem publication requires Linux flock, symlinks, atomic rename and fsync.
Generations are retained; disk usage grows and cleanup is an operator task.

Verification commands, comparisons, observed mock results, interruption behavior
and limits are recorded in deliverables/verification.md. The accuracy command is
for the supplied benchmark and paraphrase, not an evaluation of arbitrary intake
messages. It counts all 252 scalar opportunities, even when extraction fails or a
record is missing. Alternate purpose paraphrases need human source review.

The coding session is captured by the repository's enabled Entire setup and its
commit hooks. Final facilitator capture verification, a default-branch push and
Classroom root-link submission require actual external evidence; local tests do
not prove those actions occurred. Human validation of every spec line remains
the reviewer's decision.

Run the offline artifact inventory with:

```bash
python3 -m access_requests readiness https://github.com/JagdeepSSandhu/ai-full-stack-it-access-requests
```

See deliverables/submission.md for capture evidence and remaining external checks.

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
MOCKS=ROOT/'tests/mock_responses'


def operator(db, barrier):
    store=Store(db)
    barrier.wait(timeout=10)
    for number in [1,2]:
        store.ingest(read_export(ROOT/f'materials/requests/IT-{number:03}.json'),MockProvider(MOCKS))


def crash_publish(db, target):
    from access_requests.publication import publish
    publish(Store(db),target,hook=lambda stage: os._exit(17) if stage=='before_switch' else None)


class SharedTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_T32_overlap_stale_completion_and_publication_crash(self):
        from access_requests.publication import publish, read_generation
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            db=Path(td)/'state.db'
            store=Store(db)
            barrier=multiprocessing.Barrier(2)
            workers=[multiprocessing.Process(target=operator,args=(db,barrier)) for _ in range(2)]
            for p in workers: p.start()
            for p in workers:
                p.join(15)
                self.assertFalse(p.is_alive())
                self.assertEqual(p.exitcode,0)
            self.assertEqual(len(store.current()),2)
            self.assertEqual(len(store.history('IT-001.json')),1)
            target=Path(td)/'deliverables'
            publish(store,target)
            old=read_generation(target)
            self.assertEqual(old['queue'][0]['attempt_id'],old['extractions'][0]['attempt_id'])
            doc=read_export(ROOT/'materials/requests/IT-001.json')
            attempt=store.register(doc,MockProvider(MOCKS).configuration,force=True)
            claim=store.claim(attempt)
            changed=Path(td)/'IT-001.json'
            changed.write_bytes(doc['raw'].replace(b'2026-11-06',b'2026-11-07'))
            store.ingest(read_export(changed),MockProvider(MOCKS,['it-001-updated.json']))
            self.assertFalse(store.finish(attempt,process(doc,MockProvider(MOCKS)),token=claim['token']))
            self.assertEqual(store.current()[0]['extraction']['end_date'],'2026-11-07')
            worker=multiprocessing.Process(target=crash_publish,args=(db,target))
            worker.start(); worker.join(10)
            self.assertEqual(worker.exitcode,17)
            self.assertEqual(read_generation(target),old)
            publish(store,target)
            current=read_generation(target)
            self.assertEqual(current['extractions'][0]['extraction']['end_date'],'2026-11-07')
            for queue, extraction in zip(current['queue'],current['extractions']):
                self.assertEqual(queue['document_id'],extraction['document_id'])
                self.assertEqual(queue['source_sha256'],extraction['source_sha256'])

## Assumptions and limits

Operations are supported on a single host with one local SQLite database.
Overlapping processes, short transactions, fenced claims and coherent publication
are exercised; geographically distributed independent databases and network mounts
are not supported. Registration order determines the latest revision, because no
authoritative source revision sequence is supplied. History keeps prior results
separately, including success before a failed retry. Pending retries are shown
separately from completed current records, with prior errors accessible in history.

For interruption recovery, a killed worker's lease expires before another worker
reclaims unfinished work. Heartbeats renew live claims, and completed work is not
re-extracted on an unchanged rerun. Calls can repeat after a crash between provider
response and commit. Publication depends on local Linux flock, symlink, rename and
fsync behavior; an interrupted pointer switch is tested, but physical power-loss
and filesystem corruption are not simulated.

The workload assumptions come from the source's ordinary 200–400 messages and
roughly 2,000 during a surge. Worker count, timeout, retries and per-process rate
are configurable. The workload accounting checks use mocks; actual provider
capacity, real response latency, shared quotas, global rate coordination and
extraction accuracy are unmeasured. T-36 uses successful template replies; delayed
and error replies are exercised separately in T-33–T-35, not mixed into the large
batch. Rate-limit/outage recovery is simulated; real HTTP/network outages are not.

The JSON Schema validator covers the vocabulary in the supplied schema, not the
entire JSON Schema standard. Quote substring validation does not prove every model
fact is correct; independent expected facts and human review remain necessary.
The accuracy benchmark covers the 20 exports and one paraphrase. Issue coverage
uses field/category mentions, not a semantic assessment of arbitrary wording.
Policy semantic changes need corresponding routing-code changes and tests.

Generations and attempt history grow without automatic retention cleanup.
Facilitator capture/commit pairing, remote default-branch push and Classroom
submission remain external checks, not outcomes established by this suite.
